title.en: Karst cave network with vertical connectivity

summary: Compose an underground world where the interesting decisions are vertical: which chamber connects to which, and by what route.
objective: Build an explorable cave system with chambers on several levels, a water line and passages I can actually traverse.
intent_signals: Build an underground cave I can explore on foot.
Design a cave system with several levels and a water line.
example_prompts: Build a karst cave network with connected chambers, a lit entrance shaft and a flooded lower passage.
Design an explorable cave with vertical drops and a route I can follow with a lamp.
negative_signals: Not a speleological survey or a model of any real cave.
Not a geological formation simulation; growth of formations is authored, not computed.
not_for: Not a speleological survey or a model of any real cave.
Not a geological formation simulation; growth of formations is authored, not computed.

entities.name: Chamber shells
entities.guidance: Carve chambers as closed volumes with distinct silhouettes and ceiling heights; a cave made from one tube reads as a corridor, not a system.

entities.name: Connections
entities.guidance: Author each connection as a named passage with a stated traversal type: walk, crawl, climb or swim; a connection the actor cannot use is a wall.

entities.name: Formations and water
entities.guidance: Place formations where water would have run, and keep the water surface a single declared level per basin so flooded passages are consistent.

state_contract.model: Chamber graph with named passages, per-passage traversal type, a water level per basin, and an actor position with a support surface reference. Lighting state is a separate carried resource.
state_contract.authority: The chamber graph owns connectivity: if a passage is not in the graph, no visual gap may be traversable. Water level is authored per basin and is not simulated.
actions: Move between chambers along authored passages.
Raise or lower a basin water level and see which passages become impassable.
Carry, place or drop the light source.
Reset actor position, light and water levels.

invariants: Every visible opening is either a real passage in the graph or is visibly blocked.

Support and immersion decide movement, not height above a water level: the actor may stand on a dry ledge that overlooks a flooded passage, but may not stand on an inundated floor deeper than the declared wading limit or hover over water without a stated swim or boat capability.

Light is a resource with a position: illumination falls off from the lamp and can spill through an opening into an adjacent chamber, so visibility follows geometry rather than a per-chamber on or off flag.

If a basin level rises around an actor already inside a passage, the scene applies its declared rule for that case (stop, evacuate to the nearest supported cell, or an authored swim transition) rather than only blocking new entries.
motion_guidance: Constrain the actor to the cave floor with authored slope and step limits, and block movement rather than letting the camera pass through rock.
Move the light with the carrier so shadows shift as it travels; a globally lit cave loses the whole subject.
known_limits: Invented geology: formation shapes and chamber layout are art direction, not a karst process model.
Water is a static level per basin; there is no flow, drainage or infiltration model.
Authored guidance only: no scene runtime, rendering or numerical calibration has been run for this recipe.

object_craft.structure: Irregular carved volumes with distinct ceiling profiles, breakdown blocks on the floor and visible bedding planes in the walls.
object_craft.material: Damp rock family with variation in roughness between wet flowstone and dry breakdown; keep values low so the lamp is the brightest thing in the scene.
object_craft.articulation: Static geometry; only the water surface and the actor move.

object_craft.structure: Stalactites and stalagmites modelled as tapered solids with drip tips, plus rimstone pools with real lips.
object_craft.material: Translucent calcite with subsurface warmth against a colder still-water surface; both must read under lamp light alone.
object_craft.articulation: Water surface translates vertically with the basin level and clips passages accordingly.

object_craft.structure: A capsule actor with a hand-held lamp whose mount is visible, so the light has a source object.
object_craft.material: Lamp emissive plus a warm falloff; the actor material stays desaturated so the lamp dominates.
object_craft.articulation: The lamp is parented to the carrier and can be detached and left in a chamber.

physical_contract.scope: Authored walking, climbing and optional swimming on cave surfaces; no rockfall, buoyancy or hydrology.
colliders: Capsule actor against carved cave surfaces and breakdown blocks.
driving: Bounded acceleration and turn rate; climbing only at authored climb passages.
contact: Sweep movement and slide along walls; block entry to passages whose traversal type is unavailable.
physical_contract.timestep: Fixed simulation step with interpolated rendering.
checks: The actor cannot leave the cave volume at any point of an authored route.
Raising a water level blocks the passages it should and the actor is stopped there.

creative_affordances: Choose the geological character freely: fissure-dominated, chamber-dominated or a collapsed doline entrance all work.
The light source can be a lantern, a helmet lamp or a glowing organism, as long as it stays a positioned object.
